overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation for the October 3, 2018 meeting (notice sufficiently specific; post-vote discussion permitted). Allegations about the September 5, 2018 meeting were declined as untimely filed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the September 5 meeting notice topic on the code of conduct policy was insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: Since the complaints were not filed with the Board until October 16, we find the allegations relating to the September 5 meeting to be untimely and therefore decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board improperly continued discussing agenda items after votes at the September 5 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, any complaint regarding the sufficiency of the meeting notice or the impropriety of any discussion, should have been filed within 30 days of the September 5 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the October 3 notice topic 'discuss and vote on possible revisions to the Code of Conduct Policy' was insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: We find that a reasonable member of the public could read the topic “BOS to discuss and vote on possible revisions to the Code of Conduct Policy” and understand the anticipated nature of the Board’s discussion.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged it was improper for the Board to keep discussing the code of conduct at the October 3 meeting after voting to accept revisions.
allegations.key_passage: Nothing in the Open Meeting Law speaks to whether discussion may continue after a vote has been taken.
